target_customer: Dental clinics and dental insurers that review X-rays, charting and claims
problem: Dentists miss findings on radiographs and spend time on documentation, and insurers process large volumes of claims with unstructured X-rays and narratives.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to dental practices and payers, with partner and white label integrations
product_category: Dental AI imaging, documentation and claims automation

founders.name: Hamed Fesharaki
education: Bachelor of dental science, Trinity College Dublin (per YC page)
previous_startups: Open concept dental clinics in Singapore (owner, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Dentist for about a decade and owner of two clinics in Singapore per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Yasaman Nemat
previous_startups: Biotech edtech startup (name not given, co-founder)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch spells the surname Nematbakhsh and says she developed AI for hard to see cancers.

founders.name: Liushifeng Chen
founders.role: Co-founder, machine learning and computer vision
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch names him Shifeng Chen; no background stated.

competitors.name: Overjet
competitors.what: AI analysis of dental X-rays for caries and bone loss, sold to dental practices and insurers
competitors.traction_then: Reported explosive customer demand and first FDA clearance for dental AI per its Dec 2021 release
competitors.funding_then: 27M Series A about four months before its 42.5M Series B at 425M valuation in Dec 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Computer vision on dental radiographs with an FDA clearance path that TechCrunch said would take six to nine months; needs labelled imaging data and regulatory work.

defensibility.rationale: FDA clearance and accumulated labelled images are barriers, but better funded rivals such as Overjet held earlier clearances.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Dental AI rivals raised large rounds and collected most 510(k) clearances per an Innolitics analysis; Adra remained a small independent company, no acquisition found.

market_need_then: Dental imaging AI was beginning to reach clearance in 2021 and the founders were practicing dentists; pilots in a few clinics were reported in Aug 2021.

branding.domain_note: Uses adra.ai (company is also called Adravision).

identity.voice_and_tone: positions as infrastructure powering modern dentistry

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand itself; two names (Adra and Adravision) and an AI-generic .ai domain.

outcome_analysis: Adra stayed small, with about 8 people, after a 250,000 dollar raise in 2021. It reportedly won FDA 510(k) clearance for a periodontal product and now claims 512 dental teams, but better funded rivals like Overjet and Pearl raised far more. Later funding is unclear across aggregators.
notes: The 250K figure is from TechCrunch only (company stated); it includes YC money implicitly and is not confirmed by a second outlet, so treated as a round with low confidence. Aggregators conflict: PitchBook 1.6M total with a seed on 2022-03-30, CB Insights about 230K over 3 rounds, FundedIQ 100K; all unverified. FDA clearance for Adravision Perio is from a single search summary, not opened. Overjet source is dated Dec 2021, a few months after the Aug 2021 batch end; its Series A was about Aug 2021. Pearl is not listed: its Series A date was not found. Headquarters conflicts: Singapore per YC, Atlanta per CB Insights and an FDA record. Founder surname spellings differ between YC and TechCrunch.
